candidates.why: Line 1109 sets obj = &dwg->object[dwg->num_objects - 1], a raw pointer into the dwg->object array. dwg_add_object (decode.c:5464) reallocs that array and sets dwg->dirty_refs=1 (decode.c:5468), invalidating any such pointer. obj is then dereferenced at 1114/1116/1117/1118/1119/1121/1122/1123. In this specific path no further dwg_add_object occurs between 1109 and those uses, so it is only suspicious (the pattern is fragile), not proven. Note this is the #else (disabled) branch.

appctl is fetched at 1100/1101 BEFORE dwg_add_object at 1108, which may realloc dwg->object and set dwg->dirty_refs=1 (decode.c:5464-5468). If appctl->obj was cached, dwg_ref_object (dwg.c:775) only trusts ref->obj when !dwg->dirty_refs, so it re-resolves — this is guarded, but the ordering (ref obtained before a realloc-triggering add) is exactly the fragile pattern worth flagging. Disabled #else branch.

o is derived at 1132 from obj returned by dwg_ref_object(dwg, appctl) at 1126. If dwg_ref_object returned a stale cached ref->obj (dwg.c:775-776) that predates the realloc at 1108, then obj->tio.object->tio.APPID_CONTROL at 1132 would be read through a freed Dwg_Object. PUSH_HV at 1133 then writes into it. Guarded by dirty_refs in practice, hence low confidence. Disabled #else branch.

dwg_add_APPID (line 1096) expands to API_ADD_TABLE which calls dwg_add_object twice (dwg_api.c:24421/24437 via NEW_OBJECT), each potentially reallocating dwg->object (decode.c:5464). The returned _obj is a separately calloc'd Dwg_Object_APPID (dwg_api.c:22652) so it survives, and dwg_obj_generic_handlevalue recomputes &dwg->object[objid] (dwg_api.c:21831) rather than using a cached pointer — so this is safe, reported only as the closest analogue in the active #if 1 branch.
